units.text: Currently Robolectric will default to `LooperMode.Mode.PAUSED` behavior, but this can be overridden by applying a `@LooperMode(NewMode)` annotation to a test package, test class, or test method, or via the `robolectric.looperMode` system property.

quotes.quote: Currently Robolectric will default to LooperMode.Mode.PAUSED behavior, but this can be overridden by applying a @LooperMode(NewMode) annotation to a test package, test class, or test method, or via the 'robolectric.looperMode' system property.

units.text: | `PAUSED` | A mode that more accurately models real Android's Looper behavior. |

quotes.quote: A mode that more accurately models real Android's Looper behavior.

units.text: | `INSTRUMENTATION_TEST` | A mode that simulates an android instrumentation test threading model, which has a separate test thread distinct from the main looper thread. |

quotes.quote: A mode that simulates an android instrumentation test threading model, which has a separate test thread distinct from the main looper thread.

units.text: | `LEGACY` | Deprecated: use `LooperMode.PAUSED`. `LEGACY` mode is not supported on Android SDKs > Baklava. |

quotes.quote: use LooperMode.PAUSED. LEGACY mode is not supported on Android SDKs > Baklava

units.text: The upgrade guide's entries for deprecated APIs such as `Robolectric#getForegroundThreadScheduler()` say: "This is only needed in the LEGACY looper mode. We strongly encourage you to use the PAUSED looper mode (which is the default)".

quotes.quote: This is only needed in the LEGACY looper mode. We strongly encourage you to use the PAUSED looper mode (which is the default)

units.text: The Robolectric blog post "Improving Robolectric's Looper simulation" (2019) lists these highlights of the `PAUSED` mode compared with the `LEGACY` mode:

quotes.quote: Improving Robolectric's Looper simulation
Some of the highlights of the PAUSED mode vs. the existing LEGACY mode include:

units.text: - Tasks posted to the main Looper are not automatically executed inline.

quotes.quote: Tasks posted to the main Looper are not automatically executed inline.

units.text: - Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue. This is a hint that the unexecuted behavior is important for the test case.

quotes.quote: Robolectric will warn users if a test fails with unexecuted tasks in the main Looper queue. This is a hint that the unexecuted behavior is important for the test case.

units.text: - AndroidX Test APIs, like `ActivityScenario`, `FragmentScenario` and Espresso will automatically idle the main Looper.

quotes.quote: AndroidX Test APIs, like ActivityScenario, FragmentScenario and Espresso will automatically idle the main Looper.

units.text: - Tasks posted to background Loopers are executed in real threads.

quotes.quote: Tasks posted to background Loopers are executed in real threads.

units.text: The same post says: if you see test failures like `Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables`, you may need to insert `shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle()` calls to your test to drain the main Looper.

quotes.quote: If you see test failures like Main looper has queued unexecuted runnables, you may need to insert shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle() calls to your test to drain the main Looper.

import static android.os.Looper.getMainLooper; import static org.robolectric.annotation.LooperMode.Mode.PAUSED; import static org.robolectric.Shadows.shadowOf; import org.robolectric.annotation.LooperMode; @RunWith(AndroidJUnit4.class) @LooperMode(PAUSED) public class MyTest { @Test public void testCodeThatPosts() { List<String> events = new ArrayList<>(); events.add("before"); new Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post(() -> events.add("after")); events.add("between"); // the 'after' task is posted, but has not been executed yet assertThat(events).containsExactly("before", "between").inOrder(); // execute all tasks posted to main Looper shadowOf(getMainLooper()).idle(); assertThat(events).containsExactly("before", "between", "after").inOrder(); } }

units.text: The same post says under Animations: Use of Animations can cause delayed tasks to be posted to the main Looper queue. You can use the `ShadowLooper.idleFor()` or `ShadowLooper.runToEndOfTasks()` APIs to execute these tasks.

quotes.quote: Animations: Use of Animations can cause delayed tasks to be posted to the main Looper queue. You can use the
APIs to execute these tasks.

units.text: | `NATIVE` | Use graphics shadows libraries backed by native Android graphics code. |

quotes.quote: Use graphics shadows libraries backed by native Android graphics code.

units.text: | `LEGACY` | Use legacy graphics shadows that are no-ops and fakes. |

quotes.quote: Use legacy graphics shadows that are no-ops and fakes.

units.text: The Robolectric 4.10 release notes (the release that added native graphics) say native graphics "can be enabled using `@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)`. When native graphics is enabled, interactions with Android graphics classes use real native Android graphics code and are much higher fidelity."

quotes.quote: can be enabled using @GraphicsMode(NATIVE)
When native graphics is enabled, interactions with Android graphics classes use real native Android graphics code and are much higher fidelity

units.text: - 4.13: Better support for HW rendering in Robolectric Native Graphics (RNG). HW rendering is now supported all the way down to Android P. Increased compatibility with Compose's graphics layer.

quotes.quote: Better support for HW rendering in Robolectric Native Graphics (RNG)
HW rendering is now supported all the way down to Android P.
Increased compatibility with Compose's graphics layer.

units.text: - 4.12.2: In order to use HW rendering with PixelCopy, you must set the `robolectric.pixelCopyRenderMode=hardware` system property.

quotes.quote: In order to use HW rendering with PixelCopy, you must set the robolectric.pixelCopyRenderMode=hardware system property

units.text: - 4.18: Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (`@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)`) can run on Linux arm64 environments.

quotes.quote: Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments

units.text: - `SQLiteMode.Mode.NATIVE` is the default mode and does not need to be stated explicitly. `SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY` is obsolete and will be removed soon.

quotes.quote: NATIVE is the default mode and does not need to be stated explicitly.
This mode is obsolete and will be removed soon.

units.text: - The upgrade guide for 4.17 says: SQLiteMode.Mode.NATIVE is now the default, and usages of these APIs can be removed.

quotes.quote: SQLiteMode.Mode.NATIVE is now the default, and usages of these APIs can be removed

units.text: - 4.18: As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (`SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY`) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

quotes.quote: As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

units.text: - 4.18: `@TextLayoutMode` has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used.

quotes.quote: @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used

units.text: - 4.18: Native resources (`ResourcesMode.NATIVE`) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36.

quotes.quote: Native resources (ResourcesMode.NATIVE) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36

units.text: The Robolectric blog post "Designing Robolectric-based local-testing libraries for platforms and modules" describes itself as "an outside read of the code as it stands in mid-2026, not an official AndroidX position".

quotes.quote: This is an outside read of the code as it stands in mid-2026, not an official AndroidX position

units.text: - The post says the same `createAndroidComposeRule<ComponentActivity>()` / `runComposeUiTest { }` code runs on a device and on the JVM from one binary, with no Robolectric-specific source set.

quotes.quote: The same createAndroidComposeRule<ComponentActivity>() / runComposeUiTest { } code runs on a device and on the JVM from one binary, with no Robolectric-specific source set.

units.text: - The post says the only runtime detection is a single fingerprint check, and that boolean swaps one internal `IdlingStrategy` (Espresso on device; a main-thread loop that pumps Compose and forces layout on the JVM, where there is no draw pass). Frames come from a virtual-time test clock rather than a real Choreographer, and screenshot tests use Robolectric's native-graphics `PixelCopy` shadow.

quotes.quote: The only runtime detection is a single fingerprint check

That boolean swaps one internal IdlingStrategy (Espresso on device; a main-thread loop that pumps Compose and forces layout on the JVM, where there is no draw pass). Frames come from a virtual-time test clock rather than a real Choreographer, and screenshot tests use Robolectric's native-graphics PixelCopy shadow.

units.text: - The post's table says what Robolectric does for Compose UI: JVM Looper plus native-graphics shadows for rendering and PixelCopy screenshots.

quotes.quote: Compose UI JVM Looper plus native-graphics shadows for rendering and PixelCopy screenshots

units.text: - The `MainTestClock` reference says that on Android only measure and layout are performed synchronously, and that the draw pass on Android is driven by the Choreographer and will not happen as a result of forwarding this clock.

quotes.quote: on Android only measure and layout are performed synchronously. The draw pass on Android is driven by the Choreographer and will not happen as a result of forwarding this clock.

units.text: - The `MainTestClock` reference also says that if you want to assert anything related to rendering (for example `SemanticsNodeInteraction.captureToImage`) after advancing the clock, you will need a call to `ComposeTestRule.waitForIdle` or `ComposeTestRule.runOnIdle` to make sure that any triggered draw pass has been completed.

quotes.quote: you want to assert anything related to rendering (e.g. SemanticsNodeInteraction.captureToImage), you will need a call to androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.ComposeTestRule.waitForIdle or androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.ComposeTestRule.runOnIdle to make sure that any triggered draw pass has been completed.

units.text: - The Android Robolectric page says you can run other UI tests with Robolectric, such as screenshot tests. However the fidelity is lower as different devices render screens slightly differently.

quotes.quote: You can run other UI tests with Robolectric, such as screenshot tests. However the fidelity is lower as different devices render screens slightly differently.

units.text: - The Android Robolectric page recommends using Robolectric to take screenshots when the pixel accuracy is not critical, for example to test how a component reacts to different font sizes or themes.

quotes.quote: Use Robolectric to take screenshots when the pixel accuracy is not critical. For example, to test how a component reacts to different font sizes or themes.

units.text: - Robolectric can take screenshots natively, but you need a third-party library to perform screenshot testing with it.

quotes.quote: Robolectric can take screenshots natively, but you need a third-party library to perform screenshot testing with it.
